title: 5 tips you need to apply NOW to improve your static posture
summary: NH gives practical tips for static posture: a rice-filled pillow in the lower back curve when sitting, shoulders down instead of shrugged, a neutral head with the screen at eye level, a braced core and slightly tense glutes when standing, and sitting wide and open. He says posture usually degrades from the head downward and that lifting with good form fixes it long term.
claims: Most bad posture comes from habits, not birth defects like scoliosis, and takes about as many years to fix as it took to develop
The greatest long-term posture fix is lifting with proper form, which builds muscle that reinforces good posture; lifting with bad posture can cause injuries
Put a rice-filled pillow where your spine curves between upper and lower back when sitting, to hold the natural lumbar curve; rice is easier than sand and doubles as food reserve
Straight-backed chairs force your hips all the way back or leave a gap in the lower back, and 'comfortable' chairs make you round over
When reclining, move the pillow higher behind the thoracic spine
Keep your shoulders down; chronically shrugged shoulders from stress cause neck tension and trap knots
Shrugged shoulders usually roll forward too, which hurts you on presses because the shoulders aren't back in their socket
Keep the head neutral with the chin forward; raise the laptop on books to eye level and hold your phone up rather than looking down
When standing, keep a neutral spine, glutes slightly tense and core braced; this should become automatic
NH doesn't consciously brace when lifting; bracing has become automatic, and muscle itself acts as a brace
Sit wide and open, legs apart with chest up and shoulders open; closing in on yourself worsens posture and teaches your mind you aren't worth the space
Postural decline usually starts at the head, then the thoracic spine rounds, then the shoulders, then the lower back, so fix it in that order
